name: Sheraton Road and Ad Dahar
tagline: The tourist spine and the old town at the northern end
description: Sheraton Road runs the length of the resort strip with the bars, restaurants and dive centres, while Ad Dahar at the northern end is the original town with the souk, the cheaper flats and an entirely Egyptian character. The two sit within a few kilometres of each other.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the dive centres, the bars and the souk all reachable
pros: Dive centres, bars and restaurants along the strip
The old souk and local prices in Ad Dahar
cons: Persistent touting along the tourist road
Noise from the bars at night

name: El Mamsha and the Marina
tagline: The promenade and the yacht harbour, the best walking
description: The pedestrian promenade running along the water past the marina, lined with restaurants, cafes and bars, and the one part of Hurghada laid out for walking rather than driving. Apartments behind it look over the sea and the boats, at the higher end of local prices.
bestFor: Stays that want a walkable seafront and the marina restaurants
pros: A genuine pedestrian promenade along the water
Restaurants, bars and the marina at the door
Sea views from most of the apartments behind
cons: Rents above the rest of the city
Tourist pricing on food and drink
Busy and loud in the evening

name: El Kawther and El Helal
tagline: The residential districts inland, where people actually live
description: The ordinary residential quarters set back from the water, with apartment blocks, local markets, schools and a year-round Egyptian population plus a growing share of the city's permanent foreign residents. Rents here are a fraction of the seafront for a similar flat.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: Local markets and everyday shopping at Egyptian prices
cons: No sea view and a walk or ride to the water
Plain apartment blocks and dusty streets

name: Sakkala
tagline: The middle of the city, between the old town and the resorts
description: The central district between Ad Dahar and the southern hotel zone, holding the older hotels, the bus station, shops and a mix of Egyptian and tourist businesses. It is the most practical central position and cheaper than the promenade or the marina.
bestFor: Stays wanting a central position with both local and tourist services
pros: Between the old town and the resorts, close to both
Moderate rents for a central flat

name: Makadi and Sahl Hasheesh (25 km south)
tagline: The resort bays south, gated and quiet
description: The purpose-built bays south of the city, developed as self-contained resorts and residential compounds with private beaches, house reefs and their own facilities. They are quiet, well kept and entirely separate from Hurghada, which is either the appeal or the objection.
bestFor: Stays that want a private beach and a house reef, and no city at all
pros: Private beaches and excellent house reefs
cons: A car or taxis for everything outside the compound
